1 AWARD

The aforesaid four Misc. Appeals relates to the motor vehicle accident occurred in the intervening night of 26-27/08/2017 at around 12:30 A.M., at Highway within the jurisdiction of Police Station Sumerpur, District - Paali,
Rajasthan in which four members of the family lost their life.

Since common questions arises in all these appeals arising from the award passed by IIIrd Additional Member M.A.C.T, Badwani (M.P) dated 03.04.2019 in claim case Nos.368/17, 370/17, 371/17 & 372/17, therefore, same are being decided by this common award.
02. Common facts in these appeals are being narrated that all the deceased persons were travelling through Tavera Vehicle bearing registration No.MP-09-BD-4310.
On the way, Axle of Tavera vehicle got broken and it was being repaired.

On that, Container (vehicle) GJ-18-AT-8773 owned by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:28759 3 MA-4333-2019 respondent no.1 - Ravindra Kumar, driven by respondent no.2 - Amreek Singh and insured by respondent no.3 - United India Insurance Company Ltd. hit one of the passenger of Tavera vehicle namely Jagdish who succumbed to injures caused by negligent driving of respondent no.2 Amreek Singh.

03. Thereafter, Trailer vehicle No.HR-63-C-1317 owned by respondent no.4 Vivek, driven by respondent no.5 - Ramjan and insured by respondent no.6 - National Insurance Company hit Shobharam, Shyani Bai & Lavkush who succumbed to injuries.
The criminal case was registered at Police Station Sumerpur, District Pali, Rajasthan and criminal prosecution was initiated.

04. A claim case under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 was preferred by the legal representatives of Jagdish Banjara claiming Rs.51,00,000/- compensation submitting that deceased Jagdish Banjara was earning Rs.25,000/- per month as Mason and building contractor.
He was 38 years old.
Claim Case No.368/2017

was registered and claim was contested by the respondents no.3 to 6 and Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.19,45,000/- and responsibility to satisfy the compensation was fastened on respondents no.1 to 3 jointly and severally.

Being aggrieved with the amount of compensation, M.A.No.4333/2019 is preferred seeking enhancement of Rs.5,00,000/-
05.

A claim case under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 was preferred by the legal representatives of Shobharam claiming Rs.41,00,000/- on the ground that the deceased was 58 years old and was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:28759 4 MA-4333-2019 earning Rs.10,000/- per month from household work and Rs.50,000/- annually from agricultural work.

Claim Case No.370/2017 was registered and claim was contested by the respondents no.3 to 6 and Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,92,600/- and responsibility to satisfy the compensation was fastened on respondents no.4 to 6 jointly and severally.
Being aggrieved with the amount of compensation, M.A.No.6630/2019 is preferred seeking enhancement of Rs.3,00,000/-.

08. Learned counsels for the respondents/insurance company have opposed the prayer and submitted that no case for enhancement of the compensation is made out and the appeals are liable to be dismissed.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
09. Liability is not disputed.

Only quantum of compensation has to be considered, accordingly,
appeals are being considered only regarding enhancement of compensation in the light of issues raised in the appeals.
10. Firstly, M.A.No.4333/2019 arising out of the Claim Case No.368/2017 by the Third Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Badwani (M.P.) is being considered regarding death of Jagdish.
11. The tribunal assessed the income of deceased Jagdish as Rs.10,000/- per month and Rs.1,20,000/- per annum whereas the claim of the claimants was that he earned Rs.25,000/- per month.

The Tribunal discussed the issue of income in paragraph 42 of the award and estimated the income of deceased Jagdish on the basis of savings as evidenced from the passbook of saving bank account from the month of May, 2010 to June, 2017 ranging for a period of 86 months.

the Tribunal calculated average saving of Rs.5,000/- per month and assessed the income of Jagdish Banjara as Rs.10,000/-.
12.
The Tribunal adopted the proper procedure but ignored the fact that number of dependents were six.

The income could be higher in proportion to the saving, accordingly, the Tribunal ought to have assessed atleast Rs.12,000/- per month income, ought to have deducted 1/4 per person and 40%

On re-calculation, an amount of loss of dependency comes to Rs.12,000/- (per month) + Rs.4,800/- (40% future prospect) = Rs.16,800 - 1/4 (personal expenses) = 12,600/- x 12 = Rs.1,51,200/- x 15 (multiplier) = 22,68,000/-.
The tribunal has awarded only Rs.18,90,000/- in the head of loss of dependency.
Accordingly, Rs.3,78,000/- is enhanced in the head of loss of dependency 14.
The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.40,000/- in the head of loss of consortium.
The amount has been only awarded to the wife Kalabai.
The appellants no.2 to 5 are the children of deceased Jagdish and appellant no.6 Hari Banjara is the father of the deceased.
Accordingly, each of them are also entitled for loss of consortium and a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded in the head of loss of consortium.
The tribunal has not awarded any amount in the head of loss of estate.

Thus,

+ Rs.2,00,000/- + Rs.15,000/-) is further enhanced in M.A.No.4333/2019 arising out of the Claim Case No.368/2017 with the interest @ 7% per annum from the date of application i.e.20.11.2017.
The award shall be satisfied and disbursed as per the award of Claims Tribunal.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months,
the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.

17. The Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,37,600/- in the head of loss of dependency assessing the income of deceased Shobharam as Rs.4,000/- per month and adding 10%
for future prospect.

The assessed income is not the minimum wages payable to un-skilled labour,
therefore, Rs.7,125/- ought to have awarded.

18.

No amount has been awarded to the appellants no. 2 to 4 who are the children of deceased Shobharam, accordingly, an amount of Rs.1,20,000/- is further enhanced in the head of loss of consortium and Rs.15,000/- is awarded in the head of loss of estate.
